title: Attachments, archives and Vision
summary: Vision also accepts registered artifacts from verified screen.capture and screen.context receipts. Source resolution checks task membership, producer, image digest and dimensions.
html:
Attachments, archives and Vision

Desktop observations

Vision also accepts registered artifacts from verified screen.capture and screen.context receipts. Source resolution checks task membership, producer, image digest and dimensions. vision.observe describes bounded visible regions, vision.locate returns candidates and coordinates, vision.extract returns visible fields/tables with missing values and estimates, and vision.compare returns satisfied, not_satisfied or uncertain for an expected change. Use source: {"artifact_id": "returned-id"} (or an authorized context_id); compare takes before, after and expected_change. Existing vision.analyze and vision.ocr remain supported.

Locate outcomes are found, ambiguous, not_found and unreadable. Absence applies only to reviewed regions. Original-image boxes and points are projected through verified Screen geometry; eligible current PNG v2 captures produce visual_target for guarded UI actions. Confidence does not authorize an action. Titles or approximate bounds do not associate Quartz and AX identities.

Overviews use at most a 1,600-pixel long edge, followed by focused source-resolution crops when needed. Each call permits three logical model requests, including one correction, with at most two images and 4 MiB of encoded image payload per request. Outputs are bounded to 100 regions, 20 locate candidates, 200 table rows/2,000 cells and 64 KiB. Malformed/truncated output cannot produce action targets. Refinement and partial coverage remain visible in the result. Numbered annotations and selected points use the normal artifact viewer and retain source lineage.

For native qualification use scripts/desktop_vision_gateway.py --registry PATH --gateway-id ID --fixture preflight --output DIRECTORY. A reserved session can use --fixture all and the Gateway's existing desktop-capable --python interpreter. The runner creates only generated GTK or AppKit fixture windows, uses authenticated Gateway operations and the production artifact collector, and records cleanup and skipped checks. It does not request OS permissions or change saved capability settings. Fixture-oracle mechanics are distinct from model recognition accuracy.

evaluation/desktop_vision/manifest.json freezes 40 synthetic cases per workflow area, including absent and ambiguous targets. scripts/desktop_vision_evaluation.py verifies fixture digests and scores recorded results. Exact model/preprocessing metadata and Linux/macOS native workflow measurements are required; missing or skipped acceptance checks do not qualify a release. The runner stops a failed evaluation when even perfect remaining answers cannot meet a gate; remaining cases are recorded as unmeasured. Such an early stop cannot produce a passing result. Windows remains implemented; native validation pending and does not block these release gates.

An attached file has an exact context_id, recorded name, media type, size and digest. The task receives a bounded metadata manifest with a suggested reader. This makes the file discoverable without automatically reading every page or sending every image to a model. A filename or MIME label is a reader hint, not proof that the file is valid or that all of its content has been reviewed.

Use the attachment's returned context_id and reader action. If a needed skill is unavailable, request it through normal tool discovery; existing enablement and permission rules still apply. A guessed ID or a failed read does not prove that the upload is absent. Authorized references can be rediscovered through task_context.list under resources/attachments.

Choose the reader

To analyze a file on the selected Gateway, discover it with Files, then call file.attach with its exact path. The result includes a conversation-owned context_id, SHA-256, byte count, provenance and a suggested reader. For example, import a Desktop screenshot with file.attach, then pass the returned ID to vision.ocr. Vision continues to accept an attachment ID rather than a filesystem path.

Use http.download to import one HTTP(S) resource. It supports a saved profile_key or established connection_ref, the existing TLS/authentication controls, and up to five redirects by default. Credentials remain restricted to their authorized origin. It requires a Gateway advertising http_download_v1; ordinary http.request remains available on older Gateways. Both import tools return metadata without file bytes or base64, and publish only complete transfers. Directory recursion is not supported.

Settings → Maximum attachment size (bytes) (attachment_max_file_bytes in the runtime settings API) defaults to 67,108,864 bytes (64 MiB). Positive whole-byte values apply to browser uploads and both import tools. Each transfer captures its limit when it starts; changing the setting affects subsequent transfers and leaves stored files intact. Raising the limit above 64 MiB for Gateway files requires attachment_import_v1 support. Reader limits, including Vision and archive expansion, remain separate. Each active task accepts at most 16 attachments.

Imported files appear in the existing attachment chips and history. They remain with the conversation and are available to later authorized tasks, including when Task Context is disabled. Retrying a completed invocation returns the same attachment; import a changed source with a new invocation. Normal conversation deletion and cross-conversation linking rules continue to apply.

Source Explicit action Where the work happens
Supported text, code, CSV, JSON, YAML or SVG text read_context, with bounded paging and the actual encoding Controller; the returned text must fit the task's model budget.
PDF A PDF read such as pdf.info, pdf.text or pdf.render with context_id A verified working copy is transferred to the selected Gateway, which parses it.
Word, Excel or PowerPoint An Office read such as office.inspect, office.word_read or office.excel_read_range with context_id Selected Gateway after verified transfer; format-specific selection fields still apply.
PNG or JPEG image vision.ocr for text or vision.analyze for visual observations, with context_id and a prompt Controller sends bounded verified pixels to the captured image-capable model route.
ZIP, TAR or Gzip file.inspect_archive, then file.read_archive_member using an exact returned member_ref Controller; a selected member becomes a scoped attachment, without unpacking stored paths.
Unknown binary or a file needed for further tools file.open_attachment Creates a verified working copy in the selected Gateway's workspace.

Some metadata hints recognize more image extensions than Vision accepts. The current Vision decoder accepts PNG and JPEG only. Convert another format explicitly with an authorized tool; an image filename does not bypass decoding. PDF and Office mutations remain path based. To edit an uploaded document, first obtain a working copy, inspect its revision/object references and use the normal PDF or Office mutation workflow. The uploaded original is not overwritten.

Text and continuation

read_context supports UTF-8, UTF-16 little/big endian, Latin-1 and CP1252. auto uses a UTF-16 BOM when present and otherwise selects UTF-8; it does not guess Latin-1/CP1252 or accept UTF-32. Choose the actual encoding when auto is unsuitable. Invalid decoding and NUL-containing text fail explicitly. PDFs, Office files, archives and raster images require their format-aware readers.

Character allowances count Unicode characters; offsets and continuation cursors refer to the original byte representation. Successful non-UTF-8 continuation cursors also retain the selected encoding. A UTF-16 BOM counts in byte offsets but is omitted from returned text. Use the returned next_cursor, and inspect complete/has_more before claiming the whole source was read. See the Context read policy for full-read mode, deprecated byte limits and model-budget rejection behavior.

Working copies and ownership

flowchart LR U[Immutable uploaded source] --> A[Task membership and live grant check] A --> H[Verify original size and SHA-256] H --> T[Controller text or archive reader] H --> G[Unique selected-Gateway working copy] G --> D[PDF or Office operation] H --> V[Bounded image decoding and Vision request] T --> R[Receipt with source and coverage] D --> R V --> R

The attachment resolver checks current task references, linked Task Context membership when enabled, live grants and any archive-parent chain. The byte reader verifies the recorded length and SHA-256. It can load the entire upload even when the resulting text page is small; the default import/upload limit is 64 MiB and can be changed in Settings.

Working-copy transfer uses the existing artifact transfer service, a unique destination and the selected Gateway's workspace. PDF/Office reads accept exactly one of path or context_id; ordinary path calls do not trigger attachment transfer. Receipts retain source ID, digest, size and working-copy information. Missing Gateway transfer/workspace support returns an explicit locality error. It does not fall back to a Controller document parser or substitute a different Gateway.

Discovery and metadata never create access. Deleting or revoking a parent source can make its archive members unavailable. Saved filenames, copied metadata and earlier successful receipts cannot grant a different task access to the source. Context ownership covers body storage, conversation grants and deletion/recovery boundaries.

Archive limits

Inspection is bounded to 2,048 entries, 64 MiB expanded content and a maximum 200:1 expansion ratio. ZIP central-directory metadata also has a 4 MiB bound. Listings return up to 100 entries per page and include complete and next_offset. Directories, unsafe absolute/traversal names, links and encrypted ZIP members are not readable as ordinary members. The implementation does not extract members to their archived filesystem paths.

A member_ref binds the parent digest and member index. Reading it verifies the declared size, creates a child context source with parent provenance and returns the child's suggested reader. Repeated reads can reuse that child ID, but the parent is still checked. Nested archive authorization is limited to four parent levels. Read only the necessary members; a successful listing is not a review of all member contents. Source code and limits live in Files attachment tools.

Configure and use Vision

Vision is an optional, default-disabled skill with vision.ocr and vision.analyze. Configure the optional Vision role in Settings → Model routing, or use Main when no Vision connection is assigned. The selected endpoint must explicitly advertise image input; a model name alone is insufficient. Accepted tasks retain their captured routing configuration. See model configuration for per-role settings and fallback.

The Controller needs the images extra for decoding:

python -m pip install "aor-runtime[images]"
# From a source checkout:
python -m pip install -e ".[images]"

This is an explicit operator installation, not something skill discovery runs. PDF/Office parsing dependencies belong on the selected Gateway as described in their own guides. Vision does not install or start a model.

Supply a prompt of at most 4,000 characters and exactly one source form:

  • One authorized image context_id.
  • One or two artifact_ids from verified pdf.render receipts.

The latter form checks the producing operation, digest, current or linked task lineage and any original attachment grant. It does not accept arbitrary artifact images, filesystem paths or URLs. Each original input must fit within 4 MiB, and the combined metadata-free RGB PNG representations must also fit within 4 MiB. Image decoding additionally applies the shared pixel/size bounds. Render fewer pages or lower resolution when needed; the tool does not silently downscale them.

Vision sends no executable tools to the image model. Image contents are untrusted data, and responses containing tool calls are rejected. A successful observation contains source provenance, actual model-route facts, image count and coverage limited to the listed images/pages. Returned text is capped at 24,000 characters; provider length stops or excess output mark it incomplete. This is model-generated evidence with uncertainty, not an exact copy of the whole document.

The call shares the task's inference budget, cancellation and endpoint admission. An eligible configured Vision failure may use the permitted fallback to Main; Main must also support image input. After synchronous cancellation unwinds, its Controller activity is released. No delegated tool or background job is created. Original pixels remain in their source store; base64 request parts are transient and are not included in the Vision receipt.

Understand failures

Finding Next step
Reference unavailable in this task Rediscover task attachments and obtain the normal authorized reference; do not guess IDs.
Authorized source bytes unavailable Restore the original bytes or upload the source again.
Integrity check failed Use a fresh authorized source whose recorded digest matches its bytes.
Format-aware reader required Follow the returned reader/skill action instead of forcing binary content into text.
Working-copy transfer unavailable Check the selected Gateway's transfer/workspace support.
Vision does not advertise image input Configure an image-capable endpoint/model and start work with the updated routing snapshot.
Vision connection failed and Main is text-only Repair the Vision connection/model/projector, or configure an image-capable Main fallback.
Observation incomplete or over limit Narrow the page/member selection or adjust the appropriate output allowance; retain partial-coverage facts.

Implementation owners are attachment access, source adaptation, Vision tools and Vision lifecycle. Regression fixtures use generated local documents, temporary Gateway workspaces and scripted model/local HTTP responses in attachment tests and Vision routing tests; they do not require a live model or external document service.
